To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the PCB and DDT fluxes to a dated sediment core from Esthwaite Water in rural England increased sharply after the late 194os, (2) PCB and DDT concentrations in the sediment core increased exponentially with depth, (3) the PCB concentrations and fluxes to the lake were highest in the late 1970s, and (4) PCB concentrations and flux to the lake have declined since 1980, with a half-life of approximately 5 years
the most abundant PCB congeners in the dated sediment core are 28, 66, and 138.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of organochlorines in the environment, with an emphasis on the fate of persistent organic pollutants (POP) in aquatic environments.
the use of dated sediment cores to reconstruct historical inputs of organochlorine compounds to a rural English lake.
the historical input of PCB and DDT and their metabolites to a dated lacu- strine sediment core in the rural English countryside.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PCBs have been present in the environment for many centuries.
the PCBs in the sediments of Esthwaite Water are the result of a combination of atmospheric deposition and direct input from local sources.
there is little evidence that PCBs have caused adverse effects to humans, but that they have caused effects in some wildlife populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PCBs were introduced to Esthwaite Water at a time when the lake was not receiving significant amounts of agricultural runoff, and that the PCBs were introduced by atmospheric deposition, not via the water column.
PCBs were introduced to the environment at the end of the nineteenth century, and that their use in the United Kingdom increased rapidly from the 1930s, peaking in the late 1950s.
the most significant inputs to the lake occurred in the late 1950s/early to mid-1960s, when fluxes of all PCBs were high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PCBs were introduced to the environment in the 1920s.
the use of PCBs in the U.K. was very low in the early years and then increased dramatically in the late 1949s, peaking in 1970.
PCB fluxes to Esthwaite Water were low before World War II, but increased sharply after World War II and peaked in the late 1960s/early to mid 1970s.
